saints.name: St. Narcissus of Jerusalem
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A bishop of Jerusalem famed for holiness and miracles who lived to an extreme old age…
biography: Eusebius, our chief witness, presents Narcissus as already a very old man when he became bishop of Jerusalem late in the second century. He presided with Theophilus of Caesarea over a council that decreed Easter should always be kept on a Sunday, and the wonders told of him include the changing of water into oil to supply the lamps of the church at the Easter vigil.

Certain men, the same historian relates, swore false oaths against him, and though the slanders were confuted, Narcissus quietly withdrew into solitude, leaving the see to be governed in his absence by three bishops in succession. When the falsehood was exposed, the people sought him out and unanimously begged him to return.

Because of his extreme age he was given Alexander as coadjutor — the first such arrangement on record — and together they governed the church. He died about the year 216, at an age the tradition reckons far past a hundred; the Church keeps his memory on 29 October, honouring him as a model of patience under calumny and of holiness in a long episcopate.
saints.knownFor: His long episcopate and holiness at Jerusalem.
